newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Dec 23.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- AT&T Consumer Services chief quit rather than accede to John Walter's plan to replace him as part of a management shake-up.
- Many big retailers seemed resigned to Christmas sales below their earlier hopes for gains of up to 10 percent over last year.
- American General is expected to announce an accord to pay $665 million for Home Beneficial.
- Anderson Worldwide apparently decided not to split into two entities despite friction between its accounting business and faster growing consulting arm.
- Apple Computer will buy Next Software for $400 million.
- TWA is planning sharp cuts at its hub at New York's Kennedy airport.
- The Chicago Mercantile Exchange proposed increased limits on how far stock index futures can fall.
- Winn-Dixie's comparison-pricing ad policy is being referred to the FTC by the National Advertising Review Board.
- McDonald's is ordering changes to improve the taste of its burgers.
- The Fed voted to let bank holding companies collect as much as 25 percent of their total revenue from securities activities.
- ABC News reporters committed fraud by posing as Food Lion employees for a hidden camera report on the supermarket chain.
- The Air Force chose McDonnell Douglas and Lockheed Martin to compete for a $1.6 billion contract to develop rockets for launching government satellites.
- The Chicago Board of Trade was warned by regulators that it must design a new proposal for corn and soybean futures contracts by March 4.
- Texaco is meeting with the EEOC and plaintiffs' attorneys in an effort to resolve differences over last month's settlement of a race-bias suit.
- Donnkenny said the SEC is conducting a formal investigation into the apparel maker's financial statements and the trading of its securities.
- Rock-Tenn agreed to buy a Midwest packaging maker, Waldorf, for about $260 million and the assumption of about $150 million in debt.
- The issuance volume of asset-backed securities passed last year's old record of $107.9 billion on September 30 and volume should hit $141 billion this year.
- Some on Wall Street are betting that W.R. Grace is a prime takeover candidate.
-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610
